lecture_mcqs.question: Which nerve supplies the muscles of the anterior compartment of the arm?
lecture_mcqs.answer_basis: Generated for practice from the cited university lecture material; not an original lecture question.
lecture_mcqs.explanation_from_source: The musculocutaneous nerve supplies biceps brachii, brachialis and coracobrachialis.

lecture_mcqs.question: Which muscle is the primary flexor of the elbow regardless of forearm position?
lecture_mcqs.answer_basis: Generated for practice from the cited university lecture material; not an original lecture question.
lecture_mcqs.explanation_from_source: Brachialis is the main elbow flexor; biceps contribution is stronger when the forearm is supinated.

lecture_mcqs.question: Which nerve supplies the triceps brachii?
lecture_mcqs.answer_basis: Generated for practice from the cited university lecture material; not an original lecture question.
lecture_mcqs.explanation_from_source: The radial nerve supplies the posterior compartment muscles of the arm, including triceps.

lecture_mcqs.question: Which nerve is most closely related to the spiral (radial) groove of the humerus?
lecture_mcqs.answer_basis: Generated for practice from the cited university lecture material; not an original lecture question.
lecture_mcqs.explanation_from_source: The radial nerve runs in the spiral groove and is vulnerable in midshaft humeral fractures.

lecture_mcqs.question: A fracture at the surgical neck of the humerus places which nerve at greatest risk?
lecture_mcqs.answer_basis: Generated for practice from the cited university lecture material; not an original lecture question.
lecture_mcqs.explanation_from_source: The axillary nerve winds around the surgical neck with the posterior circumflex humeral artery.

lecture_mcqs.question: Which artery is particularly at risk in a supracondylar fracture of the humerus?
lecture_mcqs.answer_basis: Generated for practice from the cited university lecture material; not an original lecture question.
lecture_mcqs.explanation_from_source: The brachial artery lies anterior to the distal humerus and may be compromised in supracondylar fractures.

lecture_mcqs.question: Which bedside action is commonly used to assess anterior interosseous nerve function?
lecture_mcqs.answer_basis: Generated for practice from the cited university lecture material; not an original lecture question.
lecture_mcqs.explanation_from_source: The anterior interosseous nerve supplies flexor pollicis longus and the lateral part of flexor digitorum profundus; weakness impairs the tip-to-tip “OK” sign.

lecture_mcqs.question: Which structure is the most medial of the three major contents of the cubital fossa (lateral to medial arrangement)?
lecture_mcqs.answer_basis: Generated for practice from the cited university lecture material; not an original lecture question.
lecture_mcqs.explanation_from_source: The classic lateral-to-medial order is tendon, artery, nerve (TAN).

lecture_mcqs.question: Volkmann ischemic contracture most directly results from ischemia of which muscle group?
lecture_mcqs.answer_basis: Generated for practice from the cited university lecture material; not an original lecture question.
lecture_mcqs.explanation_from_source: Compartment ischemia can cause necrosis and fibrosis of the forearm flexors, producing wrist and finger flexion contracture.

lecture_mcqs.question: Nursemaid’s elbow is classically caused by displacement of which structure?
options: B. Radial head beneath the annular ligament
C. Olecranon beneath the ulnar collateral ligament
D. Distal radius beneath the pronator quadratus
lecture_mcqs.correct_answer: B. Radial head beneath the annular ligament
lecture_mcqs.answer_basis: Generated for practice from the cited university lecture material; not an original lecture question.
lecture_mcqs.explanation_from_source: Traction on the child’s pronated forearm can cause radial head subluxation relative to the annular ligament.

lecture_mcqs.answer_basis: Generated for practice from the cited university lecture material; not an original lecture question.
lecture_mcqs.explanation_from_source: The brachial plexus is formed by the anterior rami of C5 to T1.

pbl_cases.diagnosis_pattern: Spiral midshaft humeral fracture with wrist and finger drop, consistent with radial nerve injury near the spiral groove.
pbl_cases.summary: 65-year-old woman falls onto an outstretched abducted arm. Mid-arm deformity, swelling, tenderness and bruising; inability to extend wrist/fingers; radial pulse palpable. X-ray shows spiral midshaft humeral fracture with medial displacement of proximal segment. Wrist/finger extension recovers by ten weeks; residual shoulder stiffness is treated with physiotherapy.

osce_framework.station: Focused upper-limb neurovascular examination after humeral fracture
osce_framework.source_status: Generated from PBL and lecture material; not a complete official OSCE script.
checklist: Introduce yourself, confirm identity, explain and obtain consent.
Inspect for deformity, swelling, bruising, abnormal posture and splint.
Assess distal perfusion: radial pulse, capillary refill, colour and temperature.
Screen radial nerve: wrist/finger/thumb extension and dorsal hand sensation.
Screen axillary nerve when proximal humerus injury is suspected: deltoid contraction/abduction as tolerated and shoulder-cap sensation.
Screen median/AIN: OK sign and relevant median motor/sensory function.
Screen ulnar nerve: finger abduction/adduction and ulnar sensory territory.
Compare with unaffected limb, document findings and repeat neurovascular checks after immobilization.
limitations: Avoid forceful movement of a suspected fracture; examine within safe limits.
The lecture gives selected nerve tests, not a complete OSCE sequence.
